comment: The words each secret-leak detector is published under, one entry per
Every shell already fails if a detector reaches a contributor with no
see WORDING. Each shell hardcoded its own nine strings, so the three
could disagree about what a contributor is told is covered and nothing
would fail: a Cursor user reading 'Stripe, GitLab and Slack tokens' on
one platform and 'Cursor API keys' on another gets two different answers
This file is the single copy of those words. It lives outside every
package directory, following tests/fixtures/update-conformance/, so the
three readers cannot drift into three files.
Changing a label here is changing what the product tells contributors is
scrubbed. That is a deliberate act; the tests exist to make it one.
